title: Drenching sheep with a wormer
subtitle: How to administer oral anthelmintics and why technique affects efficacy.
excerpt: Drenching is the oral dosing of sheep with a liquid wormer via a drenching gun. Poor technique is one of the main causes of treatment failure: underdosing, dosing on a full stomach, and using the wrong drench group all reduce the kill rate and accelerate resistance. Here is the correct method and how to reduce the risk of anthelmintic resistance on your holding.
sourceNotes: SCOPS (Sustainable Control of Parasites in Sheep), Farmer Guidance (2023). NADIS, Worm Control in Sheep. Moredun Research Institute, Managing Anthelmintic Resistance.

glossaryTerms.definition: A drug that kills internal parasitic worms (helminths). In sheep, the main groups are benzimidazoles (white drench), levamisoles (yellow drench), macrocyclic lactones (clear drench), and monepantel (orange drench).

The proportion of the worm population that is NOT exposed to treatment. Worms in refugia (on pasture, in untreated animals) dilute the resistance genes of any survivors. Maintaining refugia is central to resistance management.

content.text: drench works only if the right dose reaches the right part of the gut. Sheep that are fasted before treatment (6 to 8 hours off feed) absorb the drench more slowly through the rumen, increasing contact time with worms. Sheep drenched straight from a rich grass field empty the drench through the rumen too quickly for some compounds.
Weigh a representative sample of the flock. Dose to the heaviest animal in the group. Underdosing to the average weight of a mixed group is a common cause of treatment failure.
Calibrate the drenching gun according to the product label before starting. Check the dose volume by pumping into a measuring cup.
Confirm which drench group you are using (1-BZ white, 2-LV yellow, 3-ML clear, 4-AD orange). Rotate groups between treatment events, not between years. Consistent use of one group drives resistance.
Restrain the sheep. A corner of the pen works; a cradle or sheep handler is faster for large numbers.
Insert the drenching gun nozzle into the mouth from the side, passing it over the back of the tongue. Do not force it down the throat.
Tilt the sheep's head gently upward. Administer the dose slowly. A fast bolus increases the risk of misdirection into the lungs.
Allow the sheep to swallow before releasing. Watch the throat to confirm swallowing.

by not treating every animal at every event. In a healthy flock, leave 10 to 20% of the lowest-risk animals (body condition score 3+, no scour, no weight loss) untreated. Their worm burden represents a population of untreated worms that dilutes any resistant survivors from the treated animals.
